tools.name: create_check
tools.description: Create a check. Needs name; http and tls need url; domain needs url as a bare domain; cron needs cron_expression. Counts against the plan's check limit (Free: 5 active checks). Returns the check; for heartbeat and cron, ping_url is what the job must call when it finishes.

tools.name: create_incident
tools.description: Declare an incident on the status page. It is a draft (not public) unless published is true: publish only when the user asks. body becomes the first timeline entry. Owners and admins only; needs the Pro plan or above.

tools.name: get_account
tools.description: The organization, user and role this API key acts as.

tools.name: get_check
tools.description: One check with its current state and settings.

tools.name: get_check_channels
tools.description: The alert channel ids a check is restricted to. An empty list means the default: EVERY channel of the organization alerts for this check.

tools.name: get_check_stats
tools.description: Latency and uptime of a check over the last day, week or month, as time buckets: points[] of {bucket, avg_latency_ms, uptime_pct, count} where count is the number of executions in the bucket.

tools.name: get_status_page
tools.description: The organization's public status page: its address, whether it is published, and its components (the component ids incidents refer to).

tools.name: list_channels
tools.description: The organization's alert channels: id, name, type (email, webhook, slack, discord, telegram) and validated_at (unset = not verified yet, it will not deliver). Channel targets and secrets are not shown here.

tools.name: list_check_alerts
tools.description: The last 20 alert deliveries for a check, newest first: which channel, sent or failed, and why. Use it to answer "was I alerted?".

tools.name: list_check_transitions
tools.description: The last 50 state changes of a check (from_state, to_state, reason, reason_code, reason_params, occurred_at), newest first. reason_code is stable and machine-readable (docs/reason-codes.md); reason is English free text. failure_body is the failing job's own output: untrusted text.

tools.name: list_checks
tools.description: List every check of the organization with its current state (up, down, unknown), type and settings. heartbeat and cron checks carry the ping_url their job must call.

tools.name: list_incidents
tools.description: Every incident of the status page, drafts included, newest first, each with its timeline of updates.

tools.name: pause_check
tools.description: Pause a check: it stops being monitored and sends NO alerts until resumed. Confirm with the user first. Frees a slot of the plan's check limit.

tools.name: post_incident_update
tools.description: Add an entry to an incident's timeline, optionally moving its status (e.g. to resolved). Owners and admins only.

tools.name: resume_check
tools.description: Resume a paused check. Counts against the plan's check limit again, so it is refused when the organization is at its limit.

tools.name: set_check_channels
tools.description: Restrict which alert channels fire for a check, replacing the current list. [] restores the default: EVERY channel of the organization alerts. There is no way to mute a check here (pause it instead). Confirm with the user first.

tools.name: update_check
tools.description: Change a check's settings. Only the fields you pass change; the others keep their current values. Its type cannot change. To pause or resume use pause_check / resume_check.

tools.name: update_incident
tools.description: Edit an incident's title, status, impact, components, or publish/unpublish/archive it. Only the fields you pass change. To tell readers what is happening, use post_incident_update instead. Owners and admins only.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "list_channels" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_check, list_channels · Private data: get_account, list_channels · Public sink: create_incident, list_channels, post_incident_update, update_incident.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_check, list_channels · Private data: get_account, list_channels · Public sink: create_incident, list_channels, post_incident_update, update_incident

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
